$comment: Reviewable source of truth for the live GitHub merge-boundary rules (#162).
M0 uses repository Rulesets, not classic branch protection. The fields under
`branches` retain the classic request vocabulary where it maps cleanly so the
existing offline workflow/check audit remains useful; `ruleset` records the
Ruleset-only semantics needed to reconstruct the live settings.
The live topology is topic branches -> develop -> main. `integration` is retired.
Accepted topic-branch prefixes (#381). This is the one source: README,
CONTRIBUTING, docs/WAYS-OF-WORKING.md and the workflows' push filters
are validated against it by tests/test_branch_policy.py. Push-triggered
gates must cover every prefix documented here, and PR gates run
regardless of source prefix (pull_request triggers are unfiltered).
Checks that report only on main-based PRs.
Canonical development branch. PR-gated, zero approvals, linear history.
Release/promotion branch. Ordinary changes reach main through develop -> main PRs.
One approval is required. Merge commits are intentionally allowed as release markers;
linear history is therefore not required on main. Creation is restricted.
Checks deliberately non-required must be named here with a reason.
advisory.pr-base: PR-only branch-policy check (#383): reports on pull_request events only, so it cannot be a required check that the merge queue waits on (merge_group); the correction is to rebase onto develop.
advisory.DevSkim: devskim.yml triggers on push/pull_request/schedule only, no merge_group -- same structural gap as pr-base. It runs on every develop PR but remains advisory until the owner explicitly adds it to the required merge contract; a merge-queue entry must not wait for a status this check never reports there.
